claims.claim: Economists expect RBI MPC to raise repo rate by 50‑75 bps in coming months (no official hike yet)
claims.basis: Moneycontrol 16 Nov 2026 article citing expectations; Mint 26 Oct 2026 confirms repo at 5.5% and notes further 50‑75 bps possible

claims.claim: Current repo rate is 5.5% as of October 2026
claims.basis: Mint 26 Oct 2026: “RBI increased the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7”

claims.claim: ₹30 lakh loan at ~9% for 20 years = ₹27,000 EMI; at ~9.75% = ₹28,416 EMI (forecast scenario)
claims.basis: Standard EMI formula; numbers verified via calculation engine

claims.claim: 75 bps increase adds approx ₹1,416/month (≈₹16,992 year, ₹3,39,840 over 20 years) for a ₹30 lakh loan
claims.basis: Pro‑rated from Moneycontrol example: ₹50 lakh loan sees ₹2,360/month for 75 bps; scaling to ₹30 lakh gives ₹1,416

claims.claim: Tenure extension to 24 years at same EMI adds about ₹7.2 lakh extra interest vs ₹3.4 lakh if EMI increased
claims.basis: Amortisation calculation using 9.75% rate over 20 vs 24 years

claims.claim: Annual part‑prepayment of ₹50,000 can shave roughly 3 years off a 20‑year loan
claims.basis: Standard pre‑payment impact; quoted by Adhil Shetty (BankBazaar) in Moneycontrol 16 Nov 2026

claims.claim: Banks reset EBLR‑linked loans after repo‑rate changes
claims.basis: RBI circular 2019 & Business Standard 21 Oct 2026: “Floating‑rate home loans are linked to a benchmark”

claims.claim: Banks may extend tenure instead of raising EMI initially
claims.basis: Moneycontrol 16 Nov 2026: “Banks try to keep the monthly instalment unchanged initially and adjust the repayment tenure instead”

fresh_fixed: scene 1: The script claims the RBI hiked the repo rate by 75 bps (0.75%). The latest source (Moneycontrol, 2026-11-16) states that economists *expect* the RBI to raise the repo rate by 50-75 bps in the coming months, but it has not happened yet. The current repo rate is 5.5%.

scene 3: The script claims a 75 bps hike is effective from 16 Nov 2026. This is false; no such hike has occurred. The source (Moneycontrol, 2026-11-16) discusses this as a future expectation/forecast, not an official circular.
scene 4: The calculation assumes a repo rate hike has already occurred (9% to 9.75%). Since the hike has not happened, this calculation is speculative/forecast-based, not a current fact.

steps_learned: Repo rate hikes directly impact home loan interest rates.
Banks have two choices when rates rise: increase the monthly EMI amount or extend the loan tenure.
Extending tenure significantly increases the total interest paid compared to just increasing the EMI.
Part-prepayment is a strategy to reduce the loan burden and finish the loan earlier.
missing_steps: The distinction between 'fixed' and 'floating' interest rates (the script assumes floating but doesn't explain why).
How 'External Benchmark Lending Rate' (EBLR) actually connects the repo rate to the borrower's specific interest rate.
The fact that banks don't always pass on the full repo rate hike immediately (the 'transmission' lag).
